narrative.overview: Atelix reads like a calm editorial catalog of textiles, not a transactional wholesale portal. Macro fabric photography does the persuading; the chrome around it stays quiet. A forest-green and brass palette on a warm off-white ground gives the system the composure of a well-kept reference collection. The register is product: design serves the sourcing job, and the dominant feeling is calm control over a complex, high-stakes procurement decision. Inter carries both editorial titles and functional UI, with weight and scale establishing hierarchy. Surfaces are white panels separated by hairline borders rather than heavy shadow; space is generous, density earned only where comparison demands it.
keyCharacteristics: Macro material photography as the primary visual, framed in quiet chrome
Inter hierarchy split cleanly by weight and scale (editorial vs functional)
Warm off-white ground, white panels, hairline borders; shadow only on hover
Two-signal color system: green (buyer/trust) and brass (money action/seller)
Generous space; density only where comparison requires it

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Green means buyer path + trust; brass means money action + seller. Never swap them, never use either decoratively, never add a third brand color. Blue and red are status-only and never CTAs.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px line borders and tonal panels, not shadow. Color separates meaning; borders separate space.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter carries every editorial and functional role. Use weight, scale, and spacing to establish hierarchy.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No tiny uppercase tracked kickers and no numbered section markers (01 / 02). Rhythm comes from serif headings and space.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadow appears only as a response to state — hover on a card, selection on a package.

dos: Do lead with macro material photography; the fabric is the hero, the chrome is quiet.
Do keep the Two-Signal Rule: green for buyer/trust, brass for the money action, one brass CTA per view.
Do draw structure with 1px line borders and tonal panels; reserve shadow for hover/selection state.
Do use Inter everywhere and establish hierarchy through weight, scale, and spacing.
Do surface trust at the decision point — verification badges, specs, secure-payment signals are load-bearing UI.
Do darken text toward ink to meet the WCAG AAA 7:1 target; audit muted (#6e6e68) and brass before using either for small body text.
donts: Don't build a cheap bulk-wholesale portal — no cluttered density, loud red banners, or low-trust noise.
Don't build a generic SaaS dashboard — no purple/blue gradients, glassmorphism, identical stat-card grids, or hero-metric template.
Don't chase consumer-fashion trends — no hype-drop streetwear energy or influencer aesthetics.
Don't use gradient text, background-clip:text, or side-stripe (border-left > 1px) accents.
Don't nest cards inside cards, or let resting surfaces float on shadow.
Don't add tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows or numbered section markers as scaffolding.
Don't use brass or info-blue as body text on white; brass is for fills/links (as brass-deep), blue is status-only.
